domain_label: Content Engineering — Knowledge Layering Ladder (books to cards, owner ladder mapped to theory)
purpose: A method for decomposing academic material into a five-rung knowledge-layering ladder — terminology -> basic facts -> relate two things -> compositions -> two/three-step inference — mapped onto revised Bloom's cognitive-process and knowledge dimensions, grounded in the chunking (Miller/Cowan) and worked-example (Sweller & Cooper, expertise reversal) literature, and emitting the card type appropriate to each rung, so a deck climbs from Remember to Analyze in a load-correct order rather than stalling at rote recall; every literature claim is tagged FACT (confirmed in a cited source), ESTIMATE (a stated-basis inference or a design mapping) or UNKNOWN (a named, unresolved blocker), and no exam statistic, pass rate or verbatim rule text the research file did not verify is asserted as fact.
assumptions: no observed dataset supplied; all base scores are heuristic priors

source honesty is inherited from the grounding research file: primary pages (supermemo.com, ankiweb.net, IHMC, several journals, Wikipedia) were 403-blocked this session, so FACT tags rest on search-engine snippets of the official pages and verbatim mirrors, not direct reads, and a downstream fetch-enabled run must verify verbatim wording

the owner's ladder (terminology -> basic things -> relate two things -> those two make something else -> two/three-step thinking) is a verbatim design intent; its mapping onto revised Bloom and the chunking/worked-example anchors is a design ESTIMATE (medium-high confidence), while each cited anchor is FACT
the ladder is the spine: scheduling, progress UI and card emission all key off the rung a unit of knowledge sits at, and every card is fully typed by a (Bloom process x knowledge) pair
exclusions: spaced-repetition scheduling algorithms, review intervals and the .apkg / AnkiConnect export mechanics (they belong to the scheduling specialist; this KB stops at emitting the typed card, not scheduling it)

the full Twenty-Rules card-quality canon and the bad-card lint in exhaustive form (owned by the sibling flashcard-quality KB; this KB only invokes minimum-information and the lint as they bear on a rung)
subject-matter truth of any specific textbook's content; this KB engineers the layering and card-type decisions, not the domain facts being carded
gamification, streaks and the calendar UI beyond noting that flat units can serve as calendar boxes

asserting the exact verbatim headings/glosses of all twenty Wozniak rules, any controlled image-occlusion-vs-cloze effect size, or Novak & Canas focus-question detail as fact — these are research-file [UNKNOWN]s and stay flagged

competency_questions.acceptance_condition: LADDER_SPINE names the five rungs (terminology -> basic facts -> relate two things -> compositions -> two/three-step inference) as the verbatim owner intent, states it is the spine that scheduling, progress and card emission key off, and marks the theory mapping a design ESTIMATE

competency_questions.question: Why must each rung and each card stay within a small working-memory budget, and how does the ladder respect it?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: CHUNKING_BUDGET cites Miller 1956 (~7+/-2) and Cowan 2001 (~4 focus-of-attention) as FACT, explains a chunk is a meaningful unit not an item, and LADDER_ORDER_INVARIANT shows each rung turns the previous rung's items into chunks so every question stays near the ~4-element budget

competency_questions.question: How does the ladder map onto revised Bloom's cognitive-process dimension, and where do case-based exams live on it?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: BLOOM_PROCESS_MAP gives the Remember->Understand->Apply->Analyze(->Evaluate->Create) order (Anderson & Krathwohl 2001, FACT), maps rungs 1-5 onto Remember through Analyze, and notes exam case items sit mostly at Apply/Analyze so the deck must climb there

competency_questions.question: Why is comprehension (rung 0) required before any memorizing, and what breaks if it is skipped?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: COMPREHENSION_GATE invokes Wozniak Rules 1-2 (do not learn what you do not understand; learn before you memorize, FACT via snippet) and states a rote card built without comprehension is an orphan whose grade is meaningless

competency_questions.question: What is the terminology rung and which card types serve it?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: RUNG1_TERMINOLOGY places terminology at (Remember, Factual), sources it from bold/glossary/index terms, and CARD_TYPE_SELECTION assigns basic, reversed (only if unique) and type-in cards to it

competency_questions.acceptance_condition: RUNG2_BASIC_FACTS places single atomic facts at (Remember-Understand, Factual) and MINIMUM_INFORMATION requires one card = one atomic fact so the scheduler grades one memory trace, with cloze/image-occlusion as the forms

competency_questions.question: What is a relate-two-things (edge) card and how does it map to a concept-map proposition?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: RUNG3_RELATE_EDGES places relations at (Understand, Conceptual), CONCEPTMAP_PROPOSITION equates the owner's edge to a Novak & Canas proposition (concept-link-concept, FACT for the definition; the equation is ESTIMATE), and EDGE_CARD_FAMILY gives the forward/reverse/relation/cloze card family from the triple (A,relation,B)

competency_questions.acceptance_condition: RUNG4_COMPOSITION places 'A and B make C' at (Apply, Procedural/Conceptual) and WORKED_EXAMPLE_ORDERING cites Sweller & Cooper 1985 (worked-example study cut time ~half and errors ~1/5, FACT) and the expertise-reversal caveat to fade examples into problems

competency_questions.acceptance_condition: RUNG5_MULTISTEP_INFERENCE places 2-3-edge chains at (Analyze, Conceptual), caps chains at 2-3 steps (splitting longer ones into intermediate cards per Rule 17), and KST_FRINGE frames the next reachable inference as the fringe of the current knowledge state

competency_questions.acceptance_condition: IMAGE_VS_TEXT_CHOICE cites picture-superiority/dual-coding/multimedia (FACT that the effect is robust; mechanism debated), routes spatial/structural knowledge to image-occlusion and verbal-symbolic to cloze, warns decorative images add load (coherence principle), and flags that no controlled image-occlusion-vs-cloze card study was located [UNKNOWN]

competency_questions.acceptance_condition: PREREQ_MAPPING_CHOICE lays out Option G (concept graph / Knowledge Space Theory, precise next-item selection but expensive/brittle) vs Option F (flat units, cheap/robust but no fine tracing), reflects the owner's 'graphs or maybe not' uncertainty, and recommends the hybrid: flat spine plus a lightweight edge table

competency_questions.acceptance_condition: DECOMP_PIPELINE gives the book->units->terms->claims->relations->multi-step->cards loop (each stage feeding a rung) and LAYER_COVERAGE_GATE requires the deck to climb to Apply/Analyze and to answer the book's own end-of-chapter questions, looping failures back to the claim layer

glossary.definition: The verbatim design intent: terminology -> basic facts -> relate two things -> those two make something else (composition) -> two/three-step thinking (inference). It is the spine of this KB — scheduling, progress UI and card emission all key off the rung a piece of knowledge sits at [FACT that this is the owner's intent, brief section 2a-9; the mapping to theory is ESTIMATE].

A meaningful unit of information, not an item count: immediate memory holds ~7+/-2 chunks (Miller 1956) and the true focus-of-attention limit, controlling for rehearsal, is ~4 (Cowan 2001) [FACT via snippets]. Expertise is the growth of larger chunks; each ladder rung turns the previous rung's outputs into single chunks, freeing slots for the next composition.

The six-level revised cognitive-process order Remember -> Understand -> Apply -> Analyze -> Evaluate -> Create (Anderson & Krathwohl 2001, verbs replacing Bloom 1956 nouns) [FACT via snippet]. In this KB the process dimension IS the ladder (what a question demands).

The orthogonal axis added in the 2001 revision: Factual -> Conceptual -> Procedural -> Metacognitive [FACT via snippet]. It is the CONTENT TYPE (what a KB entry is); a card is fully typed by the (process, knowledge) pair, e.g. (Remember, Factual)=term card, (Analyze, Conceptual)=multi-step case card [ESTIMATE, design mapping].

The owner's word for a relation between two concepts — the edge of a concept graph. Its literature analogue is the concept-map proposition: 'two or more concepts connected using linking words to form a meaningful statement' (Novak & Canas 2008) [FACT for the proposition definition via snippet; the edge=proposition equation is ESTIMATE, high confidence]. An edge is a triple (A, relation, B) and is only well-formed once both endpoint term cards exist.

Study a fully worked procedure before attempting problems: Sweller & Cooper 1985 found students who studied worked examples solved similar problems in ~half the time with ~1/5 the errors [FACT via snippet]. The expertise-reversal effect means worked examples lose value and can hurt as expertise grows, so fade them into problem-only variants — the rung-4-to-rung-5 transition.

Knowledge Space Theory (Doignon & Falmagne 1985, deployed in ALEKS): a knowledge state is the set of items mastered; a surmise/prerequisite relation constrains admissible learning paths; the fringe of a state is the items exactly one step ahead, of maximal diagnostic value — what to teach or test next [FACT via snippet]. It formalizes the rung-5 'next reachable inference'.

One card carries one atomic fact or relation (Wozniak Rule 4); complex answers are split into many simple items so the scheduler grades one memory trace, items are answered fast and fail independently [FACT for the principle via Rule 4 snippet; the scheduling rationale is a high-confidence ESTIMATE]. Rule 17 permits redundancy — the same fact from several angles as separate simple items.

The go/no-go that closes decomposition: the emitted deck must climb to Apply/Analyze (not stall at Remember) and must answer the book's own end-of-chapter questions; if it cannot, decomposition missed content and the failure loops back to the claim/basic-fact layer [ESTIMATE, design synthesis; the end-of-chapter-questions-as-validation-set idea rests on the OpenStax textbook-anatomy FACT].

Two reversible ways to store prerequisites from the same extracted data (terms + edges): Option G a concept graph / Knowledge Space (precise next-item selection, weakness localization; expensive, brittle if edges are guessed) vs Option F flat ordered units approximating prerequisites by 'everything earlier' (cheap, robust; no fine tracing). Owner is undecided ('graphs, or maybe not'); the recommended hybrid is a flat spine plus a lightweight edge table [FACT that owner is unsure; the recommendation is ESTIMATE].

nodes.definition: Rung 0, the implicit reading pass that precedes the ladder: understand the unit before memorizing any of it. This is Wozniak Rules 1-2 — 'do not learn if you do not understand' and 'learn before you memorize', build an overall picture first because pieces that fit one coherent structure memorize faster [FACT via search snippets of the Twenty Rules article]. A card minted before comprehension is an orphan (rote junk whose grade is meaningless); the fix is to learn the chapter first, then anchor the card to prior items. This gate is why terminology (rung 1) follows reading, not the reverse.

included: the orphan-card failure and its learn-then-anchor fix
why reading precedes the terminology rung
excluded: the terminology card forms themselves
the scheduling of the resulting cards

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a lapsing-card pattern or a comprehension-verification method changes the rung-0 gate

pros.claim: Requiring comprehension before carding stops rote orphan cards that cost huge review time for worthless knowledge
pros.example: reading a physiology section for the mechanism before making any term card, so the terms attach to an understood structure

cons.claim: A reading pass is unbilled effort a learner under time pressure may skip, and comprehension is hard to verify automatically
cons.example: a student mass-generating term cards from bold words without ever reading the surrounding argument

failure_modes: minting cards from bold terms before reading the unit, producing orphans
treating memorization as a substitute for understanding a hard passage
acceptance_tests: the analysis states Rules 1-2 as the rung-0 precondition, names the orphan-card failure, and prescribes learn-the-unit-then-anchor before any card is minted
revisit_triggers: a chronically-lapsing card traces to missing comprehension of its unit
a unit is too dense to comprehend in one reading pass and must be pre-chunked
the pipeline is caught minting cards ahead of the reading pass

nodes.definition: Establish the working-memory budget every rung and every card must respect: immediate memory holds ~7+/-2 chunks (Miller 1956) and, controlling for rehearsal, the real focus-of-attention limit is ~4 chunks (Cowan 2001) [FACT via search snippets]. A chunk is a meaningful unit, not an item count — a chess master sees configurations, not 32 pieces; expertise is the growth of larger chunks. Consequence for decomposition [ESTIMATE, direct application, high confidence]: a card's question should demand at most ~4 not-yet-chunked elements, and a study unit should introduce a handful of new concepts, not dozens. This is the load argument the whole ladder is engineered around.

excluded: the rung-by-rung invariant that operationalizes the budget (its own node)
the scheduling interval math

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a revised working-memory estimate or a per-learner chunk calibration changes the budget

pros.claim: A hard chunk budget gives an objective size ceiling for cards and units instead of vague 'keep it short' advice
pros.example: rejecting a card whose answer requires holding six unfamiliar terms at once because it exceeds the ~4-chunk focus limit

cons.claim: Chunk count is subjective — what is one chunk to an expert is four to a novice — so the budget must be read against the learner's current chunks
cons.example: assuming a formula is one chunk when a beginner still parses it symbol by symbol

failure_modes: counting items instead of chunks and over- or under-sizing a card
ignoring that a novice's chunks are smaller than an expert's when setting card size
acceptance_tests: the analysis cites Miller ~7+/-2 and Cowan ~4 as FACT, defines a chunk as a meaningful unit, and derives the at-most-~4-elements card ceiling
revisit_triggers: a card's lapse rate suggests its element count exceeds the learner's chunk budget
a newer working-memory estimate revises the ~4 figure
the learner's expertise grows enough to re-chunk prior material

nodes.definition: Map the ladder onto revised Bloom's cognitive-process dimension, the axis of what a question DEMANDS: Remember (retrieve) -> Understand (determine meaning) -> Apply (use a procedure) -> Analyze (break into components and see relations) -> Evaluate (judge by criteria) -> Create (produce new work) (Anderson & Krathwohl 2001, verbs replacing Bloom 1956 nouns) [FACT via search snippets]. Rungs 1-5 map onto Remember through Analyze, with Evaluate/Create beyond the deck's usual reach. Case-based exam items (e.g. INBDE-style vignettes) live mostly at Apply/Analyze [ESTIMATE, high confidence], so a deck that stops at Remember cannot answer them; the ladder exists to climb there.

excluded: the knowledge dimension (its own node)
the per-rung card forms

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: the target exam's Bloom-level mix or a curriculum's objective verbs change the map

pros.claim: Anchoring rungs to Bloom process levels turns a vague 'go deeper' into a named target level per unit
pros.example: labeling a unit's exam-relevant questions Analyze so the deck is built to reach analysis, not stopped at recall

cons.claim: The rung-to-Bloom mapping is a design ESTIMATE, and Bloom levels are not perfectly discrete, so a question can straddle Apply and Analyze
cons.example: a two-step application that some would call Apply and others Analyze, blurring the rung boundary

failure_modes: building a deck that stalls at Remember and cannot answer Apply/Analyze exam items
treating the Bloom levels as sharp bins when a question straddles two
acceptance_tests: the analysis gives the Remember->Create order as FACT, maps rungs 1-5 onto Remember-through-Analyze, and notes exams sit mostly at Apply/Analyze
revisit_triggers: the target exam's item level (Apply vs Analyze mix) is characterized
a unit's questions straddle two Bloom levels and need re-binning
a curriculum revises its stated objective verbs

nodes.definition: Add the orthogonal Bloom knowledge dimension — Factual -> Conceptual (interrelationships among elements) -> Procedural -> Metacognitive [FACT via snippet] — as the CONTENT TYPE of a KB entry (what it is), distinct from the process dimension (what a question demands). A card is fully typed by the pair: (Remember, Factual)=a term card, (Understand, Conceptual)=an edge card, (Apply, Procedural)=a worked-step card, (Analyze, Conceptual)=a multi-step inference card [ESTIMATE, design mapping, high confidence]. This pairing is what lets the pipeline pick a card template deterministically from a unit of knowledge.

included: the (process, knowledge) pair fully typing a card
excluded: the concrete card-template selection logic (its own node)
the process-dimension order (its own node)

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a mixed-type rule or a new template placement changes the knowledge-type grid

pros.claim: Typing a card by both dimensions makes template choice deterministic instead of a per-card judgment call
pros.example: reading (Understand, Conceptual) straight off a relation and emitting an edge card without deliberation

cons.claim: Some knowledge is genuinely mixed-type (a procedure that is also conceptual), so the pairing can force an artificial single label
cons.example: a composed procedure that is both Procedural and Conceptual and does not sit cleanly in one cell

failure_modes: assigning only a process level and leaving the knowledge type implicit, so template choice stays ad hoc
forcing mixed-type knowledge into a single cell and mis-templating it
acceptance_tests: the analysis names the four knowledge types as FACT, states a card is typed by the (process, knowledge) pair, and gives the term/edge/worked-step/multi-step exemplars
revisit_triggers: a knowledge unit resists a single type and needs a mixed-type rule
a new card template is added and must be placed in the type grid
a metacognitive-strategy card need appears

The mapping onto Bloom process levels and the chunking budget is a design ESTIMATE (medium-high confidence). nodes.definition: Establish the data-level rule that underwrites the low rungs: one card carries one atomic fact or relation (Wozniak Rule 4) [FACT for the principle via snippet]. Complex answers are split into many simple items so the scheduler grades one memory trace, items answer fast and fail independently [ESTIMATE for the scheduling rationale, high confidence — a direct consequence of per-item scheduling]. The violation symptom is a chronically half-known card whose grade is meaningless; the fix is to split. Rule 17 is a complement not a contradiction: the same fact from several angles is welcome as separate simple items. Applied at the CLAIM data level so every emitted card inherits atomicity.

included: the split fix and the half-known symptom
excluded: the specific cloze/occlusion forms (rung-2 node)
the full bad-card taxonomy (its own node)

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a chronically half-known card or an over-atomization complaint changes the atomicity rule

pros.claim: Atomic items are scheduled accurately because the grade reflects one memory trace, not a bundle
pros.example: splitting a three-part answer into three cards so a lapse localizes to the one fact actually forgotten

cons.claim: Over-atomizing can strip the context that makes an item meaningful, colliding with anchoring
cons.example: shredding a coherent definition into fragments that no longer cue each other

failure_modes: leaving an overloaded multi-answer card that grades many traces at once
over-splitting until items lose the context that made them learnable
acceptance_tests: the rule states one card = one atomic fact/relation (Rule 4), gives the split fix for the half-known symptom, and notes Rule-17 redundancy as a complement
revisit_triggers: a card is chronically half-known and must be split
an over-atomized item loses its cueing context
the claim-extraction stage emits non-atomic claims

nodes.definition: Ground the owner's 'edge' in the literature: a concept-map proposition is 'two or more concepts connected using linking words to form a meaningful statement' (Novak & Canas 2008), grounded in Ausubel's meaningful-learning theory where new knowledge attaches to existing cognitive structure [FACT for the proposition definition via snippet; the equation edge = proposition is ESTIMATE, high confidence]. An edge is therefore a triple (A, relation, B) — e.g. (lidocaine, blocks, Na+ channels); (maxillary first molar, has-root-count, 3). This is the object rung 3 produces and the unit the edge-card family and the optional graph are built from. Concept maps are built to answer a focus question [ESTIMATE, training knowledge; PDF fetch blocked].

included: the proposition definition and the edge=proposition equation
the (A, relation, B) triple form with examples
excluded: the edge card family (its own node)

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a normalization failure or a source confirmation changes the proposition schema

pros.claim: Naming the edge a proposition gives it a normalized triple form the pipeline can extract and reuse
pros.example: storing (drug, blocks, channel) once and generating several cards and a graph edge from it

cons.claim: The edge=proposition equation is an ESTIMATE, and natural-language relations resist clean triple normalization
cons.example: a hedged or multi-condition relation that does not reduce to a single clean linking word

failure_modes: treating the edge=proposition mapping as established rather than a labeled inference
forcing a nuanced multi-condition relation into a bare triple and losing the condition
acceptance_tests: the node gives the Novak & Canas proposition definition as FACT, equates it to the owner's edge as ESTIMATE, and shows the (A, relation, B) triple with examples
revisit_triggers: a relation resists triple normalization and needs a richer form

nodes.definition: Establish the instructional-order rule for the composition rung: present a fully worked example before asking for a problem solution. Sweller & Cooper 1985 found students who studied worked examples solved similar problems in ~half the time with ~1/5 the errors, because worked examples let novices acquire the schema instead of overloading working memory with unguided search [FACT via search snippets]. Caveat — the expertise-reversal effect: worked examples lose value and can even hurt as expertise grows, so they must be faded into problem-only variants [FACT via snippet]. This is exactly the rung-4-to-rung-5 transition: study the composed procedure first, then remove the scaffold.

included: the worked-example-before-problem order and its effect size
the expertise-reversal fade as the rung-4-to-5 transition
excluded: the composition rung's card content (its own node)
the multi-step inference rung

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a mastery threshold or a revised effect size changes the fade point

pros.claim: Ordering a worked example before the problem cuts novice solving time and errors by letting the schema form first
pros.example: a worked derivation card shown before the equivalent problem-only card for the same procedure

cons.claim: Worked examples must be faded or they waste an expert's time and can hurt (expertise reversal), so the order is not permanent
cons.example: keeping a worked scaffold on a procedure a learner has already mastered, slowing review

failure_modes: throwing novices straight into problems and overloading working memory
never fading the worked example and triggering the expertise-reversal cost
acceptance_tests: the node cites Sweller & Cooper 1985 (~half time, ~1/5 errors) as FACT, gives the load rationale, and prescribes fading via expertise reversal into problem-only variants
revisit_triggers: a learner's mastery grows enough to fade the worked example

nodes.definition: Formalize 'what to learn or test next' with Knowledge Space Theory (Doignon & Falmagne 1985, deployed commercially in ALEKS) [FACT via snippet]: a learner's knowledge state is the set of items mastered; a surmise/prerequisite relation (q <= q' iff mastering q' implies q) constrains which states exist and which learning paths are admissible; the fringe of a state is the items exactly one step ahead, of maximal diagnostic value. The fringe is the rung-5 'next reachable inference' and the graph option's next-item selector; a failed node localizes weakness to its prerequisites. It is powerful but expensive to build correctly and brittle if edges are guessed.

included: the knowledge-state, prerequisite-relation and fringe definitions
the fringe as next-item selector and weakness localizer
excluded: the flat-vs-graph decision itself (its own node)
the multi-step card content

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: learner data on a prerequisite edge or an adaptive-selection requirement changes the KST use

pros.claim: The fringe gives a principled next-item choice and localizes weakness to a failed node's prerequisites
pros.example: on a failed inference, testing its two prerequisite edges to find which one is missing

cons.claim: Building a correct knowledge space is expensive and brittle when prerequisite edges are guessed rather than validated
cons.example: a mis-specified prerequisite edge routing a learner to an item they are not ready for

failure_modes: guessing prerequisite edges and shipping a brittle knowledge space
over-engineering full KST for linear material that a flat order would serve
acceptance_tests: the node defines knowledge state, prerequisite relation and fringe (Doignon & Falmagne / ALEKS, FACT), casts the fringe as the next-item selector, and states the expensive/brittle caveat
revisit_triggers: a guessed prerequisite edge is contradicted by learner data
adaptive next-item selection is demanded and justifies full KST

nodes.definition: Rung 1, terminology: the (Remember, Factual) layer where the vocabulary is learned. Source it for free from the textbook's bold terms, back-of-book glossary and heavily-indexed terms (the index is a concept-frequency signal — hub terms are the ones to learn first) [FACT that these features exist via OpenStax front-matter snippets; the harvesting leverage is ESTIMATE]. One record per term: name, definition, optional image. Chunk formation begins here — each learned term becomes a chunk the higher rungs can compose. This rung is served by basic, reversed (only if the back uniquely identifies the front) and type-in card templates.

included: chunk-formation-begins-here and the term card templates
excluded: the reversed-card uniqueness rule detail (card-type node)
the basic-facts claims of rung 2

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a hub-term discovery or a harvest miss changes the terminology layer

pros.claim: Harvesting bold/glossary/index terms yields the terminology layer almost for free and flags hub concepts
pros.example: pulling every bold term and its glossary definition into term cards, prioritizing the heavily-indexed hubs

cons.claim: A term card with no understood context is an orphan, so rung 1 depends on the rung-0 comprehension pass
cons.example: a definition card memorized as a string with no idea of what the term does

failure_modes: carding terms before comprehension, producing orphans
auto-reversing a term card whose definition is shared by several terms, manufacturing interference
acceptance_tests: rung 1 places terminology at (Remember, Factual), sources it from bold/glossary/index terms, and assigns basic/reversed/type-in templates
revisit_triggers: a term proves to be a hub with many edges and needs prioritizing

nodes.definition: Rung 2, basic facts: the (Remember-Understand, Factual) layer of single atomic statements — one subject, one predicate, one value — extracted as claims so cards inherit atomicity at the data level. Each claim is stamped with its source (Rule 18) and, if volatile, its collection date (Rule 19) so statistics do not silently go stale; for this factory every emitted card also carries its KB source id [FACT on Rules 18/19 via snippet; the KB-id policy is a house ESTIMATE]. The forms are cloze deletion (a short hidden span in a context-bearing sentence) and image occlusion where the claim is spatial. Governed by the minimum-information principle.

included: source/date stamping and the KB-source-id policy
cloze and image-occlusion as the forms

nodes.definition: Rung 4, 'those two things make something else': the (Apply, Procedural/Conceptual) layer where two related items compose into a third — a derived quantity, a procedure, an outcome. nodes.definition: Decide image/occlusion vs text cloze at a rung. Mayer's multimedia principle: people learn better from words + pictures than words alone. Practical rule [ESTIMATE, synthesis]: use image/occlusion when the knowledge IS spatial/structural (anatomy, apparatus, chart positions, flow order), cloze when it is verbal-symbolic (definitions, numbers, names); decorative images add extraneous load, not memory (coherence principle). Left [UNKNOWN]: no controlled image-occlusion-vs-cloze card study was located, so the routing rests on generic picture-superiority evidence, not a card-format A/B result.

nodes.definition: State and defend the invariant that makes the rung ORDER load-correct [ESTIMATE, high confidence, resting on the Cowan FACT]: each rung's outputs become single chunks at the next rung, keeping every question within the ~4-chunk working-memory budget. edge_cases.trigger: an unordered set is carded as a single answer
edge_cases.mitigation: convert the set to an enumeration (impose order/grouping) then the enumeration to per-element clozes (Rules 9-10)

edge_cases.description: A volatile statistic card carries no collection date and is silently wrong a year later
edge_cases.trigger: a rung-2 claim is extracted without a date stamp
edge_cases.mitigation: date-stamp volatile facts (Rule 19) and source-stamp all claims (Rule 18) with the KB source id so they can be updated

edge_cases.description: A cloze deletion leaves an ambiguous stem where five similar facts could fill the blank
edge_cases.trigger: the remaining sentence does not uniquely determine the hidden span
edge_cases.mitigation: tighten the stem so the answer is unique (Rules 11-12) and add a discriminating context cue

edge_cases.description: An inference chain runs to four or five steps and overloads working memory as one card
edge_cases.trigger: a derivation longer than 2-3 steps is asked whole
edge_cases.mitigation: split the chain into intermediate cards (Rule 17 blesses memorizing derivation steps) so no card exceeds the budget

edge_cases.description: The worked-example scaffold is never faded and slows an already-expert learner (expertise reversal)
edge_cases.trigger: a mastered procedure keeps its worked solution attached
edge_cases.mitigation: fade the worked example into a problem-only variant once the schema is formed

edge_cases.description: A decorative image is added to a verbal-symbolic card and adds extraneous load without aiding memory
edge_cases.trigger: imagery is applied where the knowledge is not spatial
edge_cases.mitigation: reserve images for spatial/structural knowledge and drop decorative ones (coherence principle); keep verbal facts as cloze

edge_cases.description: An edge card is minted before one of its endpoint terms has been learned as a term card
edge_cases.trigger: a relation is carded ahead of its prerequisite terminology
edge_cases.mitigation: require both endpoint term cards to exist before the edge card is well-formed; defer the edge until they do

edge_cases.description: The deck answers all term and fact cards but cannot answer a single end-of-chapter case question
edge_cases.trigger: decomposition stalled at Remember and never built rung-4/5 cards
edge_cases.mitigation: no-go until the deck climbs to Apply/Analyze; loop back to the relations stage and compose multi-step cards to cover the held-out questions

edge_cases.description: A full concept graph is built for linear material (e.g. grammar drills) that a flat order would have served
edge_cases.trigger: the graph option is chosen for material with no branching prerequisites
edge_cases.mitigation: use the flat spine plus edge table for linear material and reserve full KST for genuinely branching prerequisite structures

edge_cases.description: A snippet-confirmed rule gloss is asserted as the exact verbatim wording of the source
edge_cases.trigger: a 403-blocked primary page's wording is quoted as verbatim fact
edge_cases.mitigation: mark snippet-confirmed claims FACT-via-snippet, keep exact verbatim and un-located studies [UNKNOWN], and schedule a fetch-enabled verification pass

workflow.action: Read the unit for comprehension before carding
workflow.description: Do the rung-0 reading pass so terms and facts attach to an understood structure (Rules 1-2)
workflow.gate: the unit is understood as a structure before any card is minted, avoiding orphan cards

workflow.action: Fix the working-memory budget and the ladder spine
workflow.description: State the five rungs, map them onto Bloom process levels, and set the ~4-chunk budget every rung must respect
workflow.gate: the five rungs plus rung-0 are named, mapped to Bloom (ESTIMATE) and tied to the chunk budget (FACT)

workflow.action: Type each knowledge unit by the (process, knowledge) pair
workflow.description: Assign a Bloom process level and a knowledge type so its rung and template are determined
workflow.gate: each unit carries a (process, knowledge) pair that its rung and template read off

workflow.description: Pull bold/glossary/index terms into term records and prioritize hub terms
workflow.gate: terminology is placed at (Remember, Factual) with hub terms flagged and term templates assigned

workflow.description: Extract one-subject-one-predicate-one-value claims, source/date-stamp them, and form cloze/occlusion cards
workflow.gate: claims are atomic (minimum information), source/date-stamped (Rules 18-19), and carry the KB source id

workflow.description: For every multi-term claim, normalize an edge triple and emit the edge card family
workflow.gate: each edge is a (term_a, relation, term_b, unit_id) triple with both endpoint terms already learned

workflow.description: Write 'given A and B, what follows?' with the worked solution first, then a problem-only variant
workflow.gate: each composition is placed at (Apply, Procedural/Conceptual) with a worked example ordered before the problem

workflow.description: Chain 2-3 edges/compositions into case/vignette cards, splitting longer chains into intermediate cards
workflow.gate: chains are capped at 2-3 steps (Rule 17 splitting) and every term in them is already a chunk

workflow.action: Select the card template per rung and the image-vs-text form
workflow.description: Read the template off the (rung, type) pair and choose occlusion vs cloze for spatial vs verbal claims
workflow.gate: each rung's template is assigned by rule, reversed cards gated on uniqueness, and spatial claims routed to occlusion

workflow.action: Lint the emitted cards for the bad-card patterns
workflow.description: Split overloaded cards, convert sets to enumerations to clozes, and run a deck-wide interference check
workflow.gate: no overloaded or whole-set cards remain and interference is checked across the whole deck

workflow.action: Choose the prerequisite storage (graph vs flat) and run the pipeline
workflow.description: Store edges as a flat spine plus lightweight edge table (upgradable to KST) and run book->units->...->cards
workflow.gate: edges are stored in the reversible flat-plus-edge-table form and the six pipeline stages have each fed their rung

workflow.action: Gate coverage and depth before shipping
workflow.description: Confirm the deck climbs to Apply/Analyze and answers the book's end-of-chapter questions, tracing every card to a source
workflow.gate: the deck climbs to Apply/Analyze, answers the held-out end-of-chapter questions, and asserts no [UNKNOWN] as fact

priority_rationale: The comprehension gate, chunking budget and the Bloom process and knowledge dimensions come first because the whole ladder is a mapping of the owner's rungs onto those anchors and every card is typed by the (process, knowledge) pair; the ladder spine, minimum-information, concept-map proposition, worked-example ordering and KST fringe next, because they are the theory objects each rung is built from; the five rungs then apply them in order (terminology, basic facts, edges, composition, inference) since each rung chunks the one below it; the card-form nodes (template selection, image-vs-text, edge family, bad-card lint, order invariant) then turn a rung into an emitted, linted card; and the prerequisite-mapping choice, decomposition pipeline and layer-coverage gate come last because they compose every upstream output into a book-to-cards loop and a defensible climb-and-cover go/no-go.

dominance_rules.rule: The rung order dominates authoring convenience
dominance_rules.rationale: each rung chunks the previous within the ~4-chunk budget, so a skipped rung leaves a higher card failing for the wrong reason
dominance_rules.trigger: a plan proposes jumping straight to inference cards
dominance_rules.action: enforce mastery at each rung first; do not emit a rung-5 card whose terms are not already chunks

dominance_rules.rule: The chunk budget dominates card size
dominance_rules.rationale: the focus-of-attention limit is ~4 chunks (Cowan), so a question demanding more overloads working memory
dominance_rules.trigger: a card's answer requires holding more than ~4 unchunked elements
dominance_rules.action: split the card or push its prerequisites to lower rungs until each question fits the budget

dominance_rules.rationale: a card built without understanding is an orphan whose grade is meaningless (Rules 1-2)
dominance_rules.trigger: cards are being minted before the unit is read
dominance_rules.action: do the rung-0 reading pass first and anchor each card to prior items before memorizing

dominance_rules.rationale: a reversed card whose back is shared by several fronts manufactures interference (Rule 11)
dominance_rules.trigger: auto-reverse is applied to a term or edge card
dominance_rules.action: emit the reverse only when the back uniquely identifies the front; otherwise suppress it

dominance_rules.rationale: chains longer than 2-3 steps exceed the budget and fail for reasons other than the target logic
dominance_rules.trigger: an inference card runs to four or more steps
dominance_rules.action: split it into intermediate cards (Rule 17 blesses memorizing derivation steps)

dominance_rules.rule: Climb-and-cover dominates a tidy shallow deck
dominance_rules.rationale: exams live at Apply/Analyze, so a Remember-only deck fails the exam however clean its term cards are
dominance_rules.trigger: the deck answers term/fact cards but no end-of-chapter case question
dominance_rules.action: no-go until it climbs to rung 4/5 and can answer the held-out questions

dominance_rules.rationale: the primary pages were 403-blocked, so verbatim wording and un-located effects are not confirmed
dominance_rules.trigger: a rule gloss or effect size is about to be stated as verbatim fact
dominance_rules.action: mark it FACT-via-snippet, keep exact wording and un-located studies [UNKNOWN], and require a fetch-enabled verification pass

dominance_rules.rationale: decorative images add extraneous load without memory benefit (coherence principle)
dominance_rules.trigger: an image is proposed for a verbal-symbolic card
dominance_rules.action: use images only for genuinely spatial/structural knowledge and drop decorative ones

anti_rework_rules.rule: Do the rung-0 comprehension pass before minting any card
anti_rework_rules.prevents: orphan cards that must later be deleted or relearned once the unit is finally understood

anti_rework_rules.rule: Extract claims atomic and source/date-stamped at the data level
anti_rework_rules.prevents: re-splitting overloaded cards and hunting sources after the deck is built

anti_rework_rules.rule: Require both endpoint term cards before emitting an edge card
anti_rework_rules.prevents: premature edge cards that fail and must be pulled until their terminology exists

anti_rework_rules.rule: Gate every reversed card on back-uniqueness when it is generated
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a wave of interference-manufacturing reverse cards being cleaned up across the whole deck later

anti_rework_rules.rule: Cap inference chains at 2-3 steps and split longer ones up front
anti_rework_rules.prevents: rebuilding overloaded multi-step cards into intermediate cards after they lapse

anti_rework_rules.rule: Extract the edge table even when shipping flat units
anti_rework_rules.prevents: re-extracting relations from scratch to upgrade the flat spine to a concept graph later

anti_rework_rules.rule: Hold out the end-of-chapter questions as a validation set before authoring
anti_rework_rules.prevents: discovering post-hoc that the deck cannot answer the book's own questions and re-decomposing

anti_rework_rules.rule: Tag every literature claim FACT-via-snippet / ESTIMATE / UNKNOWN as it is written
anti_rework_rules.prevents: an unverified verbatim or effect-size claim propagating into cards and being retracted after a fetch-enabled check

iteration_protocol.trigger: a fetch-enabled run confirms the exact verbatim Twenty-Rules wording or the full Anki note-type list
iteration_protocol.action: replace the FACT-via-snippet and ESTIMATE tags on the affected claims with confirmed FACT and correct any wording

iteration_protocol.trigger: a controlled image-occlusion-vs-cloze card-format study is located or run
iteration_protocol.action: replace the [UNKNOWN] card-format routing with the measured result and re-tune the image-vs-text decision

iteration_protocol.trigger: review data shows a higher-rung card failing because of a missing lower rung
iteration_protocol.action: re-check the rung order invariant and the prerequisite completeness for that unit

iteration_protocol.trigger: adaptive next-item selection is demanded by the product
iteration_protocol.action: upgrade the flat-spine-plus-edge-table store to a validated Knowledge Space and activate fringe-based selection

iteration_protocol.trigger: the target exam's Bloom-level mix (Apply vs Analyze) is characterized
iteration_protocol.action: re-tune the climb requirement and the proportion of rung-4/5 cards the coverage gate demands

iteration_protocol.trigger: a source lacks standard textbook anatomy (no objectives, glossary or end-of-chapter questions)
iteration_protocol.action: substitute an alternate unit-parse and coverage-validation target in the pipeline and gate

iteration_protocol.trigger: a deck-wide interference pair surfaces across units in review data
iteration_protocol.action: reword the pair for contrast, add discriminating context cues, and update the bad-card lint

required_checks: all edge ids unique EDGE_XXX format
all from/to in edges reference valid node ids
all competency_question_refs resolve to valid CQ ids
all evidence_refs resolve to valid source_registry ids
all priority_order entries are valid node ids with no duplicates
high_risk_nodes (risk_if_wrong>=0.80) have non-empty acceptance_tests and human_review_required=true
conflict edges have signed_tension<0 and resolution_rule present
observed_impact=0.0 for all nodes (no observed data)
19-24 nodes, 32-40 edges, 8-10 conflict_axes, 10-12 edge_cases, 9-12 workflow steps
post_formula_checks: all derived fields non-zero after compute run

validation_report.notes: built by kb_forge.py; run validators/kb_validator.py --mode dense to certify

test_cases.input_summary: smallest meaningful instance in this domain

evaluation_suite.regression_policy: re-run evaluation suite after any node addition or formula change
